title: T3 timeout on upstream ranging
shortDescription: Motorola modem got no response from the CMTS to upstream ranging within 200 ms.
fullDescription:
Motorola-branded cable modems (MB series, MG series) log T3 timeouts when upstream ranging attempts go unanswered. Most commonly caused by loose coax, faulty splitters, or low upstream signal levels.

If T3 errors occur in bursts followed by modem reboot, expect intermittent internet. Persistent T3 indicates line work needed.

fixSteps.title: Tighten all coax
fixSteps.instruction: Hand-tight plus 1/8 turn wrench on each connector.

fixSteps.title: Remove splitters
fixSteps.instruction: Connect modem direct to wall for testing.

whenToCallPro: When signal levels are out of spec after DIY steps.

faq.q: Is a Motorola MB7621 good for 400 Mbps?
faq.a: Yes, it supports DOCSIS 3.0 at up to ~650 Mbps.

title: T1 timeout - no SYNC message received
shortDescription: Modem failed to receive SYNC messages on downstream within the T1 window.
fullDescription:
T1 timeouts mean the Motorola modem cannot find or lock onto a downstream DOCSIS channel. Downstream LED typically blinks endlessly.

Check for completely absent signal, damaged coax, or ISP outage.

fixSteps.title: Check outage status
fixSteps.instruction: Call ISP outage hotline before home troubleshooting.

fixSteps.title: Swap coax cable
fixSteps.instruction: Try a fresh RG6 direct to the wall.

whenToCallPro: No signal at wall after fresh cable - ISP tech visit required.

faq.q: What does a blinking downstream LED mean?
faq.a: The modem is searching for a signal - expected for ~1 min at boot, not constantly.

title: Online light off despite sync
shortDescription: Modem has DS/US sync but cannot complete provisioning/registration.
fullDescription: When Power, Receive and Send LEDs are solid but Online is off, the Motorola modem is signal-synced but not authorized by the ISP. Most common cause: modem not provisioned on the account.

fixSteps.title: Self-activate
fixSteps.instruction: Visit ISP activation page from a cellular-only device.

fixSteps.title: Call ISP with MAC
fixSteps.instruction: Provide modem MAC from sticker to register.

whenToCallPro: ISP must provision the modem.

faq.q: Do all ISPs accept Motorola modems?
faq.a: Check your ISP's approved modem list first.

title: Stuck scanning downstream
shortDescription: Modem endlessly searching for a lockable downstream channel.
fullDescription: Modem's receive LED blinks as it scans. Caused by missing or weak downstream signal, damaged coax, or a bad splitter.
whenToCallPro: No signal at wall - ISP line tech needed.

faq.a: DOCSIS 3.0 supports up to 32 DS channels; 3.1 models bond multiple OFDM blocks.

title: DHCP lease not obtained from ISP
shortDescription: WAN-side DHCP request unanswered after ranging completed.
fullDescription: Motorola modem cannot pull a WAN IP from the ISP DHCP server. Often an account/provisioning issue or a stale lease.

fixSteps.title: 60-second power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug modem for a full minute.

whenToCallPro: ISP to clear stuck lease.

faq.a: No - this is the WAN side between modem and ISP.

title: IPv6 prefix not obtained
fullDescription: Motorola modems on some ISPs fail to register an IPv6 prefix after a firmware change or ISP provisioning update.
whenToCallPro: Persistent after firmware push - upgrade to DOCSIS 3.1 model.

faq.a: Yes, DOCSIS 3.1 models fully support IPv6.

title: Modem operating in partial service mode
shortDescription: Some bonded channels failed to register; modem operating on fewer channels.
fullDescription: The CMTS marked one or more bonded channels unusable. Modem stays online but at reduced speeds. Usually caused by an impaired channel due to ingress or plant issue.
symptoms: Fewer bonded channels shown in UI
whenToCallPro: Persistent partial service requires ISP line work.

faq.q: How do I tell I'm in partial service?
faq.a: Check modem status page - fewer channels listed than advertised.

title: CMTS rejected registration
shortDescription: CMTS returned a registration failure to the modem's REG-REQ.
fullDescription: The modem completed ranging and DHCP but the CMTS refused to register it, typically because the configuration file was invalid or the CMTS could not load it.
whenToCallPro: Always ISP-side fix.

faq.a: No - only the ISP can push a valid configuration file.

title: Modem overheating / thermal reboot
shortDescription: Hot modem reboots randomly, especially in warm weather.
fullDescription: Motorola MB7621 and MB8600 generate significant heat. In a closed cabinet or hot room the SoC throttles and the modem reboots, causing brief internet loss.

fixSteps.title: Move to open space
fixSteps.instruction: Place modem vertically with 6 inches clearance on all sides.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed - this is a DIY ventilation issue.

faq.q: Is it safe to run warm?
faq.a: Warm is fine - hot enough to be uncomfortable to touch means you need airflow.

title: Modem dead after electrical storm
shortDescription: No LEDs at all or stuck on power only after a storm.
fullDescription: Surges on the coax line or power line can destroy the modem's tuner or PSU. Non-surge-protected modems are especially vulnerable. If only Power LED lights and no signal ever arrives, suspect surge damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace modem
fixSteps.instruction: Surge damage is usually terminal - get a replacement with coax surge protector.

whenToCallPro: If you want an electrician to install whole-home surge protection.

faq.a: Often yes - check your policy for electrical surge coverage.

fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, factory-reset and reconfigure.
